newsitem.title: USA: USAir Group to rename itself US Airways in 97.
newsitem.headline: USAir Group to rename itself US Airways in 97.

text.p: USAir Group said Tuesday that it is renaming itself US Airways as a "major expression of its evolving position among domestic and international airlines."
USAir said the name change will become effective early next year, along with newly painted aircraft bearing the U.S. flag as its symbol.

"This is an airline that has made great strides in recent months in its operational efficiency, in the development of its international route structure and in its financial performance," said USAir Chief Executive Stephen Wolf. "It is time to say to the world, and to ourselves, who we are and what we intend to become."

USAir recently announced plans to end its code-sharing agreement with British Airways in March 1997. The carrier is suing British Airways, which has a 24.6 percent stake in USAir, and AMR Corp's American Airlines over their plans to develop a transatlantic alliance.
Also on Tuesday, USAir said said its order of up to 400 aircraft from Airbus Industrie depends on it being able to achieve a competitive cost structure.

The order includes 120 firm orders and 160 open-ended orders for narrow-body aircraft with a common engine type that would replace four different types of older aircraft with three engine types, the carrier said.
USAir declined to comment specifically on the cost of the corporate name change and new image, but said it will require a "limited amount of money stretched out over three years."
